transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-02
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (Agora CTO), Leila Chen (Product), Samir Patel (Platform)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): Discussed open model candidates and deployment paths; emphasis on multilingual support, context length, and tool-calling for internal knowledge connectors. Action items captured.

[00:00] Jordan Kim: hey everyone thanks for carving out time, uh I'm Jordan from Redwood, this is Priya our solutions engineer. quick agenda — understand your workload, context length, model requirements, and security constraints.
[00:17] Marco Ruiz: yep thanks Jordan, we wanna make sure we pick a path that doesn't box us in — current thought is open models but we need to validate latency and cost. we run a knowledge assistant for internal ops and a public-facing help chat.
[00:34] Leila Chen: hi all — product here. main asks: multi-lingual for en/es/pt, and the chat has long sessions where customers paste transcripts (20–30k tokens), so context is a big deal. also want tool-calling to hit internal ticketing system.
[00:52] Samir Patel: and from infra, we have strict encryption requirements, SSO via SAML, and we'd prefer VPC options for production. open to hosted for initial pilot.
[01:10] Priya Shah: great — couple clarifying q's: when you say 20–30k tokens are you expecting that as full raw context every request, or do you do retrieval + summarization?
[01:24] Marco Ruiz: mostly raw, customers paste long transcripts, but we could pre-process; however we want the model to reference original text for accuracy. retrieval in combination would be ideal but we need >20k effective context or a KV-cache to stitch earlier messages.
[01:42] Jordan Kim: makes sense. On models — are you leaning to specific open families? some folks pick Mistral-32k, Llama-3-70b-32k variants, or a Falcon-like model. cost and latency differ a lot.
[01:58] Leila Chen: we've been looking at Mistral for gen quality, but concerned about latency at scale. also heard Llama-3 has good instruction tuning.
[02:12] Marco Ruiz: and internal concerns: can we do private (on-prem) eventually? compliance team will ask for audit logs and KMS integration.
[02:25] Priya Shah: Redwood supports three modes — Hosted API for rapid pilot, Dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput and isolation, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for strict controls. For a pilot we usually recommend Hosted + Dedicated proof points, then migrate to Private if needed.
[02:45] Samir Patel: what's the latency delta between hosted and dedicated? and how does batching affect synchronous chat?
[02:54] Priya Shah: with Dedicated you get dedicated GPU pools: lower variance and predictable p99. Hosted is multi-tenant but we have performance profiles; batching reduces cost but adds latency — we can tune batching thresholds per route. For chat with human latency targets (sub 600 ms token p99) we often recommend dedicated inference paths or smaller model variants.
[03:18] Marco Ruiz: ok, makes sense. any recommendations for quantized models vs float32 for quality? we care about hallucinations.
[03:27] Priya Shah: quantization (int8/int4) gives big cost savings, often with negligible quality drops depending on model. for hallucination-sensitive tasks we run evals on your prompt set; sometimes Llama-3 variants calibrated with 8-bit quantization preserve quality, but we should test.
[03:45] Leila Chen: about multilingual — do tokenizers handle es/pt well across these models? we have a decent Spanish corpus and some Portuguese.
[03:53] Priya Shah: tokenizer behavior varies: some open models do better out of the box; retrieval + embeddings often helps. Redwood can recommend model/tokenizer pairings given a sample corpus.
[04:05] Jordan Kim: quick question on tool-calling — Leila mentioned calling internal ticketing. do you need function-calling with structured outputs or simple webhooks?
[04:14] Leila Chen: structured outputs — we have a ticket create API that expects JSON with fields. also we want to surface citations back to the user.
[04:23] Priya Shah: Redwood's streaming and function-calling support will let you call functions and return structured JSON; we also support tool plugins patterns. We'll need to design safe execution policies for private data.
[04:34] Marco Ruiz: security checklist — SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS for key management, audit logs, and data residency (EU). are those all supported?
[04:44] Jordan Kim: yes — Hosted has SOC2 and supports SAML/SSO, Dedicated adds network isolation and private peering, Private gives full VPC/on-prem control and can integrate with customer KMS/HSM. we'll share docs.
[04:56] Speaker 1: (misc) also note retention controls, redaction pipelines can be added pre-ingest.
[05:06] Samir Patel: for retrieval — we use vector DB today (open source) and want embeddings that match. any constraints on embedding models / compatibility?
[05:16] Priya Shah: Redwood supports embeddings pipelines and stores token-level cost; we can recommend an embedding model for your vector store and run similarity tests.
[05:25] Leila Chen: ok, back to cost — can you ballpark cost difference between Mistral-32k hosted vs Llama-3-32k dedicated?
[05:35] Jordan Kim: rough rule: Mistral models are often cheaper compute per token, but it depends on GPU kernel optimizations; Dedicated has a fixed monthly for reservation plus lower per-token. we'll send a detailed matrix.
[05:48] Marco Ruiz: perfect. also need to talk about billing seats and rate limits — our product team wants predictable budgets.
[05:57] Jordan Kim: we can set quotas per API key and token caps; Dedicated is easiest for predictable billing.
[06:06] Priya Shah: technically, a few deep-dive points we'd like to validate in the next call: 1) end-to-end 32k prompt run time and p99 latencies on your sample prompts, 2) hallucination/regression tests on your safety prompt set, and 3) tool-calling flow with structured JSON returned and retries.
[06:25] Marco Ruiz: yes that sounds good. we'll compile a test set and share.

[06:40] (short pause, coordinating)
[06:55] Samir Patel: small infra note — we prefer private peering for Dedicated if possible; are there region constraints? we have EU data residency requirements.
[07:07] Priya Shah: Dedicated can be provisioned in supported cloud regions; Private on-prem/VPC supports EU residency. for Hosted we have EU regions too. we'll flag locations in the docpack.
[07:22] Leila Chen: What about versioning and rollouts? we need to pin model versions and do canary deployments so we don't break prod.
[07:31] Priya Shah: Redwood supports model version pinning, canary rollouts, and automatic fallback to smaller or older model variants. We can wire tracing hooks to your telemetry.
[07:46] Marco Ruiz: another question — prefix/KV caching mentioned earlier; how transparent is that to application?
[07:53] Priya Shah: we expose caching primitives and automatic prefix caching; Redwood Optimize gives suggestions when caching will benefit cost/latency. KV cache is managed by the runtime but you can control TTLs.
[08:07] Jordan Kim: quick caller note — any blockers on your side to start a pilot? timeline?
[08:13] Leila Chen: timeline: we'd like a pilot in the next two weeks, run for 2–4 weeks, then decide. stakeholders: security (internal), infra, product. cost approvals might take extra time.
[08:27] Marco Ruiz: agreed. pilot goals: validate 32k context viability, latency targets under 700 ms token p99 for interactive, and correct tool-calls to ticketing system 95% success.
[08:40] Priya Shah: noted — we'll draft a benchmark plan and share.

[09:00] (jump ahead — technical asides)
[09:05] Priya Shah: on model picks: recommend testing Mistral-32k and Llama-3-70b-32k quantized. Also consider a smaller Llama-3-13b for warm paths to hit latency. For multilingual, test with your Spanish plus Portuguese prompts; tokenization quirks sometimes surface with names and mixed language.
[09:28] Samir Patel: what about hallucination mitigation patterns? we want source attribution and to reduce confident false answers.
[09:36] Priya Shah: combine retrieval with grounding prompts, use citation-enabled output, and run evals with your prompt set. Redwood has tooling to detect regressions and surface quality deltas after quantization or model swaps.
[09:50] Jordan Kim: also experimentation: we can route low-latency traffic to smaller variants and fall back to larger context variants for heavy sessions.
[10:01] Marco Ruiz: curious on how function-calling is authenticated when calling our internal APIs.
[10:07] Priya Shah: functions can run via an integration layer; for private deployments we can set up secure connectors in VPC with mTLS and tokenized calls. For Hosted we provide secure proxies and short-lived tokens.
[10:21] Leila Chen: any red flags on our side? we just need clear docs and a quick onboarding path for the pilot.
[10:28] Jordan Kim: no red flags — we'll send a pilot checklist and security pack.

[10:40] (wrap-up)
[10:42] Jordan Kim: recap: Redwood to share pricing matrix, SOC2/SSO/KMS docs, and a benchmark plan. Agora to share prompts, sample transcripts, and ticketing API spec. schedule a technical deep dive next week to run the 32k tests.
[10:58] Marco Ruiz: thanks — we'll get the materials to you this week.
[11:05] Leila Chen: thanks everyone, excited to move forward.
[11:10] Jordan Kim: awesome, we'll follow up with calendar invite and docs.
[11:15] (meeting ends)
